solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal scoffs at abandoned people

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of the next two words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain sneers at people society has turned its back on.
explanation.definitionFit: Castoffs are people rejected or discarded by others, so the phrase describes them exactly.

clue.text: In hearing is one who's hacked storage device

indicators.note: in hearing tells the solver to go by how the words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: to hack is to cough harshly, so one who has hacked is a cougher

explanation.surface: Reads like a story about a computer hacker breaking into a storage drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacked' pulls toward computer crime, but here it means coughed; a cougher sounds just like the strongbox word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox for keeping money or valuables, a storage container in the plainest sense.

clue.text: I can't get enough of it!

definitions.text: I can't get enough of it!

parts.words: I can't get enough of it!
parts.note: the cry of someone with an insatiable appetite; the unnamed 'it' is a coy stand-in for sex

explanation.surface: An enthusiast's exclamation about some unnamed pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone addicted to sex would say exactly this of it, the unnamed 'it' being the activity they crave.

clue.text: Smell that makes you open up door

indicators.note: opening up the word door breaks its letters apart so they can be rearranged
the clue has the rearranged door take in the letter for you, so it surrounds that letter

parts.note: U is the text-speak spelling of you

explanation.surface: A whiff that tempts you to throw the door open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open up' rearranges DOOR to ODOR, and U (you) goes inside it before the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, usually a noticeable or unpleasant one.

clue.text: A nasty novel started with fine daydream

indicators.note: the clue says the rearranged letters begin with the letter for fine, so it goes in front

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of 'A nasty' are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grim book that opened pleasantly enough with a dreamy reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges A NASTY into ANTASY, after F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy is an imagined, wishful scenario, the same as a daydream.

clue.text: Markets filled with 100 measuring devices

indicators.note: filled with says the first word's letters take another piece inside them

parts.note: markets as in trade or selling, the sense of sales figures
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Shops stocked with a hundred weighing machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales are instruments for weighing, a kind of measuring apparatus.

clue.text: I'll let loose with chess, securing fourth file without issue

indicators.note: securing means the jumbled letters hold another letter inside them
letting the letters loose frees them to fall into a new order

parts.note: on a chessboard the files are lettered a to h, so the fourth is d

explanation.surface: A chess player ranting about freeing pieces down the d-file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' signals the anagram; chessboard files are lettered a to h. 'Issue' means offspring here, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language issue means offspring, so dying without issue means having no children.

clue.text: On ecstasy and last of gin, young guy gets loaded

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the young man comes first

parts.note: a lad is a young man
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of gin

explanation.surface: A lad who has taken pills and gin ends up drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means carrying a heavy load, a synonym of loaded.

clue.text: Small nuclear weapon, but making a very loud sound

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Trident is the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A modest warhead that still goes off with a deafening roar.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the name of Britain's nuclear missile system.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident describes a harsh, loud, grating noise.

clue.text: Beastly sort discovered eating animal hearts

indicators.note: eating has the first word swallow the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to have discovered something is to have found it
an ox is a farm animal
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A cruel creature found devouring the hearts of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A foxhound is a hunting dog, an animal type, so 'beastly sort' is a playful description of the breed.

clue.text: Hot slice from Domino's put in woman's hamper

indicators.note: put in tells us these pieces are placed inside the woman's word

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
hot in the sense of fashionable, which is also in

indicators.note: a slice from the pizza chain's name is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A pizza slice tucked into a woman's picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb. 'Hot' gives IN (fashionable), not H.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinder is to obstruct or hold back, the verb sense of hamper.

clue.text: Ultimately, this will cut blubber

indicators.note: will cut means that letter slices into the blubber word

parts.note: blubber is whale fat, so fat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word this, its final letter

explanation.surface: A slogan promising a diet will eventually shed the pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: going without food does cut fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without food for a period reduces body fat over time, which the clue calls cutting blubber.

clue.text: Film husband turned over on Sky

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: turned over means the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: re means concerning or on, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A husband switches the TV to a film on Sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster, which makes the surface about television.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether is the clear upper sky or heavens, a poetic term for the air above.

clue.text: Wild party held in a bar by Scottish delinquent

indicators.note: held in says the party sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A rowdy party thrown in a pub by a Scottish tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A NED is a Scottish young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned behaviour is unrestrained and uninhibited, which is what wild means.

clue.text: Out of shape bishops must have whip- round!

indicators.note: round says the whip word goes around the bishops

parts.note: to flay is to whip or flog
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two bishops are BB

explanation.surface: Overweight clergy must pass the collection plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round', a British term for a collection of money, is split: 'round' is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby means soft and fleshy, lacking muscle tone, so out of condition.

clue.text: I can give you a shot of noble hugging a soprano

definitions.text: I can give you a shot

indicators.note: hugging means the noble wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman
per means a or each, as in miles per hour
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A noble embraces an opera singer and offers a taste of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER (as in 'ten pounds a head'). 'Shot' means a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who serves behind a bar pours shots of spirits for customers.

clue.text: Very concerning having to cover up a crime

indicators.note: covering up the letter means wrapping the other pieces around it

parts.note: très is French for very
on means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A worrying conspiracy to hush up an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: TRES is French for 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is one of the gravest offences in law.

clue.text: In need of movement? Old prunes dazzle!

indicators.note: letters needing movement are to be rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Stale dried fruit, helpful to the constipated, is somehow dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Need of movement' hints at prunes as a laxative, but it rearranges OLD PRUNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificent brilliance, the noun sense of dazzle.

clue.text: Huge celebrity mates rag to get into shape

indicators.note: getting letters into shape means arranging them into a new form

explanation.surface: A famous star's friends tease them into going to the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is an exceptionally famous performer, bigger than an ordinary star.

clue.text: Passage, but inclusive second stage of trip

indicators.note: inclusive means the first word takes in the next letter

parts.note: but in the sense of except, as in 'all but one'

indicators.note: the second stage of a word is its second letter

explanation.surface: A travel itinerary noting the next leg of the journey is included.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is an extract from a text, which is what a passage is.

clue.text: Fish head served up with aromatic starter

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: starter takes the opening letter of aromatic

explanation.surface: A fish head served with a fragrant appetiser.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, a common example of the category.

clue.text: A sailor after the first edition of Brighton Rock

indicators.note: after places the A and the sailor behind the letter from Brighton
the first edition of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor seeks a first edition of Graham Greene's novel Brighton Rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton Rock is a Graham Greene novel and a seaside sweet, so 'Rock' hides as part of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, an example of rock.

clue.text: Outlaw with seniority squeezing last of salad dressing

indicators.note: squeezing means the other pieces press around the letter

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
age brings seniority

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of salad

explanation.surface: A senior outlaw squeezing out the final drops of salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad dressing' looks like one thing, but 'dressing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a dressing for a wound, the medical sense rather than the culinary.

clue.text: A primarily sceptic philosopher is full of doubt

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of sceptic

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A sceptical philosopher is riddled with doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askant is to look askance, with suspicion or mistrust.

clue.text: Old king soon to arrest courageous maiden

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the soon word holds the others inside

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
game means brave and willing
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler is about to detain a brave young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: I'm told they might long for loads of space

indicators.note: I'm told signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it, so those who long are achers

explanation.surface: Gossip about people yearning for wide open spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres, as in 'acres of room', is idiomatic for a great expanse of land or room.

clue.text: Awful underwear

definitions.meaning: British slang for rubbish or terrible
in Britain the word means underpants rather than trousers

explanation.surface: A verdict on some dreadful lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the word is both slang for something rubbish and the everyday name for underpants.

clue.text: Good article on old music producer

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning good
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A favourable piece about a veteran record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a record-industry figure, but it means an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano produces music, a playful description of the instrument.

clue.text: Heroin and speed found on tense singer

indicators.note: found on puts the drug and speed after the tense letter

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
H is slang for heroin
to rush is to go at speed

explanation.surface: A nervous singer is busted with heroin and amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like the drug, but it gives RUSH, and the singer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, so a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Famous player on a drama broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-known actor appears in a televised drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests an actor, but it is the Argentine footballer Diego Maradona.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona was one of the most famous footballers ever to play.

clue.text: Take exception to host losing head

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter of the host word

parts.note: to host a show is to present it

explanation.surface: Objecting to a presenter being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel aggrieved by it, to take offence at it.

clue.text: Protest singer hampering conservative US politician?

indicators.note: hampering means the conservative letter is hemmed in between the other pieces

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
a rat or informer sings to the police

explanation.surface: A protest singer heckling a Conservative US politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the politician's party is the opposite of conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of the two major US parties.
